# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 13 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 13

**13:1** And when she was in her sixth month, Joseph came from his buildings and entered his house and found her with child. And he struck his face and threw himself on the ground upon sackcloth and wept bitterly, saying: "With what face shall I look toward the Lord God? What prayer shall I make concerning this maiden? For I received her out of the temple of the Lord God as a virgin, and I have not kept her. Who has set this trap for me? Who has done this evil in my house and defiled her? Has the story of Adam been repeated in me? For as Adam was away in the hour of his prayer and the serpent came and found Eve alone and deceived her — so also has it happened to me."

**13:2** And Joseph arose from the sackcloth and called Mary and said: "You who were brought up in the Holy of Holies and received food from the hand of an angel — why have you done this? Why have you forgotten the Lord your God? Why have you humbled your soul?"

**13:3** But she wept bitterly, saying, "I am pure, and I know not a man."

**13:4** And Joseph said to her, "Whence then is that which is in your womb?"

**13:5** And she said, "As the Lord my God lives, I do not know from where it came to me."

---

## Translator's Note

Joseph's extended lament in 13:1 contains the remarkable Adam-Eve analogy — the only place in early Christian literature where the Annunciation is implicitly compared to the Fall, with Joseph (absent) in the role of Adam. The comparison serves the narrative: it presents Joseph as innocent of complicity and Mary as victimized in her absence (though the text does not ultimately frame it that way). Mary's double assertion "I am pure, and I know not a man" is the text's clearest virginity declaration. Her answer in 13:5 — "I do not know from where it came to me" — is theologically charged: she genuinely has forgotten the angelic message (cf. 12:3).
